title: Behavioral neuroscience: motivation, emotion, sleep and stress
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how the brain and body produce the drives and states that organize behavior: homeostasis and the hypothalamus, hunger and thirst, hormones and behavior, sexual behavior and its development, emotion and the amygdala, fear learning, stress and the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis, reward and addiction, sleep and its stages, circadian rhythms, and the neural basis of social behavior.
primary_reading: Neuroscience Online, an open-access textbook from McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston (free)

weeks.11: Social behavior and its neural basis
weeks.12: Comparing species: what animal studies can tell us about people

blocks.deliverable: Explain a feedback loop that regulates intake.
Evaluate a supplied study on hormones and behavior.
Design an experiment that separates two theories of emotion.
Week 7 midterm; trace the stress response from threat to cortisol and back.
Model sleep pressure and the circadian rhythm with two simple curves.
Weigh the evidence from animal models for one human behavior.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Behavioral neuroscience review: write a review article of about 2,500 words on one motivated state or emotion (for example fear, hunger, sleep or social bonding), covering its neural circuits, hormones, animal and human evidence and open questions, with a critical discussion of how well the animal findings apply to people.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
